newsitem.title: FRANCE: French child sex raids cause suicides, revulsion.
newsitem.headline: French child sex raids cause suicides, revulsion.

text.p: France's biggest ever crackdown on paedophiles has triggered three suicides, ensnared teachers and priests and led to national revulsion tinged with doubts about an orgy of public shaming.

Minister of Youth Marie-George Buffet pledged to reinforce controls at schools, youth clubs and summer camps after teachers formed one of the biggest groups among 210 people placed under investigation on suspicion of viewing child sex videos.
"The ministry has been very vigilant for a long time. We will reinforce that," she told the daily France-Soir on Saturday.

Since Tuesday, about 2,500 police have raided hundreds of homes of people who had ordered videos featuring boys aged under 15 from a mail-order company in the central city of Macon, normally best known for its Burgundy wines.
But the deaths of three men who hanged themselves after being questioned by police triggered criticisms that France had gone too far in publicly pillorying suspects.
"These huge anti-paedophile raids are scandalous, they destroy and dishonour people," said Henri Leclerc, head of the League of Human Rights. "We must keep a sense of proportion."

He said people viewing videos involving child sex were not comparable with such figures as Belgium's Marc Dutroux and Patrick Derochette, between them accused of abusing and murdering five young girls.
An unemployed, 37-year-old handicapped man killed himself in Givors, near Lyon, on Friday. He had been detained during the police investigation but released for lack of evidence.

An unnamed 48-year-old bachelor, an executive at an arms factory in central France, hanged himself on Thursday. "I can't take it. Forgive me, big kisses to the family," the daily Liberation said he wrote in a suicide note.
And a postal inspector in his 40s was also found hanged at his home in the eastern town of Saint-Martin-d'Heres on Thursday after police questioned him about pornographic materials at his home.

The French daily Le Monde said in a commentary on Saturday entitled "To Die of Shame" that the suicides "raised fears...that we have gone from one danger to another, from the era of silence to that of branding with a red-hot iron".
The suspected ringleader, Bernard Alapetite, the 47-year-old head of a Paris publishing house, is among about 20 people in pre-trial detention.
Police said Alapetite copied foreign child sex videos -- featuring rapes of boys aged under 15 and even sex with animals -- and sold them for 800 francs ($140) each.
